items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good 'what if' geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: rise with real curiosity on every question, say every number with genuine amazement, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. Say 'again?' in the first line with a playful, knowing lift. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level throughout. Pronounce 'Iberia' as 'eye-BEER-ee-uh'.
lines: Narrator
What if Spain and Portugal became one country... again?
Narrator
Yes, again. They've already done it once.
Narrator
In fifteen eighty, Portugal's royal family ran out of heirs.
Narrator
So Spain's king took the crown... for sixty years.
Narrator
So what would this country get today?
Narrator
About sixty-one million people... more than Italy.
Narrator
Two languages spoken by over eight hundred million people.
Narrator
And a Nobel-winning writer already picked its name: Iberia.
Narrator
So why did Portugal walk away?
Narrator
Spain kept dragging Portugal into its wars.
Narrator
So on December first, sixteen forty, Portugal took its crown back.
Narrator
And it still gets a day off for that.
Narrator
But that's not even the weirdest part.
Narrator
Cross the border today... and you travel back in time.
Narrator
Spain's clocks run an hour ahead. Since nineteen forty.
Narrator
Then there's the capital. Madrid... or Lisbon?
Narrator
And Portugal has just one demand.
Narrator
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
